newsitem.title: GERMANY: Sievert - Buba gold plan to impact debt, deficit.
newsitem.headline: Sievert - Buba gold plan to impact debt, deficit.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Olaf Sievert said on Thursday a revaluation of Germany's central bank gold reserves, a move under discussion by Bonn, would impact the country's debt and deficit levels.

Finance Minister Theo Waigel has said he will consider revaluing the Bundesbank's gold reserves in line with market prices, a move he said would free up funds to help Bonn cut debt to qualify for European monetary union.
"As far as we aware, Waigel plans to use these returns to retire more debt. Such a procedure would affect deficit and debt criteria," Sievert said at a news conference.
Sievert said profits made from revaluing the gold reserves could be treated like tax income, which can be used to reduce both debt and deficit levels.
He added, however, that revenue from selling shares in German telephone group Deutsche Telekom AG would be treated differently and could only be used to reduce debt.
